Outline: The scarred man’s inspection concludes abruptly. He steps back from Caelen, his demeanor shifting from clinical assessment to something colder, more dismissive. He gestures toward the girl again, this time with a sharp jerk of his chin, signaling for her to move or perhaps to be removed. The guard, previously frozen, reacts instantly, pulling a heavy iron keyring from his belt and shuffling over to Caelen’s shackled wrists. The collar around Caelen’s neck clinks as the guard fumbles with the locking mechanism, testing its strength. Meanwhile, the girl begins to weep silently, her small hands digging into Caelen’s arm until her knuckles turn white. Caelen realizes the man in purple has not intervened; the scarred man is acting on his own authority within this pen, and his judgment appears final. The beat ends with the guard successfully unlocking the shackles but leaving them loose for a moment—a deliberate delay—and the girl looking up at Caelen with a desperate, uncomprehending hope.
Prose:
After the cane left Scarface stood offering his hand out once again palm up. Both offering and indicating Caelen should stand.   

Beneath him, the girl began to weep. She made no sound, only small, hitching gasps that vibrated through her chest. Her fingers dug into Caelen’s forearm, nails pressing deep enough to draw blood, anchoring him as if she feared he would dissolve into the stone floor. He looked down at her face, pale and streaked with soot, eyes wide and wet.

She was looking for a savior, or perhaps just someone who understood why she was crying. But Caelen saw only the man in purple sitting near the ledger, his cane tapping idly against the floor, completely absorbed in whatever thoughts occupied him. Scarface stood between them now, a wall of scars and silence.

Every eye in the cell focused on him.

Caelen tried to stand, to pull himself up on the loose shackles, but the girl’s grip held him down. He realized then that shielding her had not saved her; it had only made him transparent, exposing every vulnerability to the eyes of those who ruled this place.

With a gentle voice with those same tones of soothing, he comforted the girl until her grip relaxed and he was able to stand. The patience of the cell was astounding. No one had moved no one had said anything they just waited and watched. They acted like they had an endless amount of time.  Caelen had to reflect that is nothing else imprisonment taught patience.
